about: How every feature survives a machine being off (doc 91). One entry per feature in features.json (fitness 'continuity-declared' fails on a missing one). needs: what a node must have for the feature to work at all; full: what it needs to work at its best. Both are lists of card checks (any node in the scenario that has all of them is enough). state: replicated (the same on every node), stateless (each node serves it alone), per-node (works anywhere, but its data stays on the node that made it), single-home (its data lives on one node only). when_off: what a person sees when no node can provide it fully. fix: what removes the single point of failure.

checks.strong_ai: a cloud AI key, or a model machine (a GPU box)
checks.online: the online tunnel (your own addresses from anywhere)
checks.backups: a clean backup from the last 2 days

capabilities.when_off: Your Life OS data is on every node; the PWA also keeps a copy on each device.
capabilities.fix: ./securax nodes invite (a second node holds the same data)

capabilities.when_off: Part of the Life OS: on every node.
Reading runs on the laptop that holds the papers; the actions it made are in the Life OS on every node.
The scan reads on your phone; the captured note is in the Life OS Inbox on every node.
The lens runs entirely in the browser on your phone; what it learned is on the device and syncs with the Life OS.
Assessments are files on the machine that made them; the backup carries them; the board pack is a plain HTML file that opens anywhere.
Each node syncs with whichever others answer.
Every node has its own gateway; without a key or a model machine it answers with its own small model.
capabilities.fix: ./securax keys (on each node: a free key)

capabilities.when_off: New chats work on any node. Past chat history stays on the node it was written on (shared history is dated in doc 86).
capabilities.fix: ./securax keys on each node; shared history: doc 86

capabilities.when_off: The answer rules apply on every node; a small model says so on its answers.
Building runs on any node; with no key it uses the local coder model.
Your own addresses (hub, chat) are reached through any node that runs the tunnel. With none on, use the node's local or Tailscale address.
capabilities.fix: ./securax online invite (run its line on a second machine)

capabilities.when_off: The Bitwarden apps keep an offline copy, so you can still read your passwords; saving new ones waits until that node is back.
capabilities.fix: keep the password manager on the machine that is always on (the VPS): ./securax start passwords there, then move the data with ./securax backup and ./securax restore

capabilities.when_off: Each node backs up what it holds. A node with no recent backup loses up to the age of its last one.
capabilities.fix: ./securax routines install (nightly backups) and ./securax backup offsite on each node

capabilities.when_off: A clean copy must exist away from the machine that was hit.
capabilities.fix: ./securax protect and ./securax backup offsite on each node

capabilities.when_off: The plan and its drills run on any node.

Any machine reads the same wheel and gives the same weekly lever; the Saturday message needs the routines on the always-on machine.

The idea library ships with the estate, so any machine gives the same week's idea; the seen ledger is per-machine, so a spare machine may re-show an idea the main one already sent, and the Wednesday message needs the routines on the always-on machine.
The catalog and templates ship with the code on every machine; your own answers live in that machine's vault.

reference.about: The estate SecuRAX is designed for: a laptop, a VPS and a cloud instance, each set up as the docs say. In CI no critical feature may stop working when any ONE of them is off, except what 'accepted' lists with a reason and a review date.

accepted.passwords: One password server: two would not sync with each other. The Bitwarden apps keep an offline copy for reading. Review 2027-01-31 (a standby that restores the nightly backup).
